title: Noise pollution alters the body or behavior of 80% of animal species studied, a Science analysis finds
tldr: A pooled analysis of 214 experiments on 177 species found human-made noise changed physiology or behavior in eight of ten species and cut animal numbers by about 37% in noisy areas.

title: Parkinson's may be driven by a vicious cycle that clogs the brain's waste drainage
tldr: Misfolded alpha-synuclein appears to inflame the lymphatic vessels that drain the brain, which then clear it less well, in human tissue and mice.
byline: New Scientist, Journal of Experimental Medicine (study)

title: FDA grants accelerated approval to a subcutaneous antibody for previously treated head and neck cancer
tldr: The FDA granted accelerated approval to Rybrevant Faspro for recurrent or metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma after chemotherapy and immunotherapy, based on a 42% response rate in 102 patients.

title: A hair and 1,000 seeds from a Siberian tomb give the oldest directly dated evidence of cannabis intoxication
tldr: Archaeologists found about 1,000 cannabis seeds and hair carrying a breakdown product of THC in a Scythian princely tomb in Siberia, dated to the early eighth century B.C., in a study in Science.
byline: University of Bern, New Scientist, Scientific American

title: British health worker with Ebola flown home as the Congo outbreak passes 10,000 cases
tldr: A British healthcare worker infected in DR Congo is being evacuated to the UK, the first British case of an outbreak that has passed 10,000 confirmed cases and has no approved treatment.

title: Comprehensive mapping of essential-gene interactions in M. tuberculosis
tldr: Researchers built the largest map yet of how essential genes interact in the tuberculosis bacterium, finding nearly 6,500 interactions that could guide new drug targets and antibiotic combinations.
byline: Isaac J. Kresse, Natalie Y. Sayegh, Vanisha Munsamy-Govender et al. · Rockefeller University

title: The global geography of threats to freshwater biodiversity
tldr: A global analysis of 45 threats to more than 21,000 freshwater species finds farming, dams and agricultural runoff dominate, and that freshwater species face higher threat on average than land species.
byline: Christophe Brabant, Laura Pollock, Jonas Geldmann et al. · McGill University

title: Prone positioning and high-frequency oscillatory ventilation in early paediatric acute respiratory distress syndrome (PROSpect): an international, two-by-two factorial, response-adaptive, phase 3, randomised controlled trial
tldr: A large international randomized trial found no evidence that prone positioning or high-frequency oscillatory ventilation improves ventilator-free days in children with early, moderate-to-severe acute respiratory distress syndrome.
byline: Martha A Q Curley, Martin C J Kneyber, Ira M Cheifetz et al.

title: First measles death in New York State in 30 years
tldr: A child in Lewis County, New York, died of measles, the state's first measles death in 30 years, as US cases reach their highest level in about 35 years.

title: FDA finalizes potency guidance for cell and gene therapies
tldr: The FDA issued final guidance telling makers of cell and gene therapies to build a plan proving that every batch is potent before it reaches a patient.

title: English A&Es to use early warning scores for sick children
tldr: NHS England is introducing a vital-signs scoring system for children in emergency departments this winter, with parents' concerns able to trigger urgent review regardless of score.

title: TAVR in Patients with Moderate Aortic Stenosis with At-Risk Features
tldr: In a randomized trial of 744 older adults with moderate aortic stenosis and risk features, early valve replacement cut two-year death or heart failure events from 23.9% to 16.7%.
